facts.value: A new computational tool for the analysis of floor borne vibrations on the performance and image quality of MRI scanners

evidence.claim: Developed a Python finite element framework for MRI scanner vibration and magneto-mechanical analysis.
evidence.detail: Framework uses NGSolve/Netgen and covers coupled electromagnetic and structural simulation.
Implemented magnetostatic, time-harmonic, transient, modal and coupled analyses.

evidence.claim: Developed magnetostatic and eddy-current electromagnetic formulations for MRI-relevant models.
evidence.detail: Work includes low-frequency electromagnetic modelling and coupled magneto-mechanical effects.

evidence.claim: Implemented and used linear elastic, modal and vibration analyses in coupled engineering models.
evidence.detail: Structural dynamics is a central part of the MRI vibration work.

evidence.claim: Verified numerical formulations using analytical and manufactured solutions, convergence studies and reference models.
evidence.detail: Verification spans electromagnetic, mechanical and coupled solver components and includes ANSYS comparisons.

evidence.claim: Ran computationally demanding 3D studies with approximately three million mechanical degrees of freedom.
evidence.detail: Used multi-core workstations and the Sunbird / Supercomputing Wales HPC environment.

evidence.claim: Used Linux, SLURM and Apptainer for high-performance computing workflows.
evidence.detail: Experience includes job submission, computational campaigns and reproducible environments.

evidence.claim: Developed a maintainable scientific software codebase with automated tests and Git-based workflows.
evidence.detail: The repository includes 44 automated unit, characterisation and regression tests in the referenced CV version.

evidence.claim: Worked with geometry, meshing, material regions, interfaces and boundary conditions for complex simulation models.
evidence.detail: Includes STEP/OpenCascade workflows in industrial 3D magnet modelling.

evidence.claim: Collaborated with Siemens Healthineers on MRI magnet simulation cases and industrial reference comparisons.
evidence.detail: Translated numerical modelling results into engineering insight and validation work.

evidence.claim: Performed topology optimisation of a Formula Student car bulkhead using ANSYS Mechanical.
evidence.detail: Structures-team work targeted a lighter design while retaining structural performance.

evidence.claim: Conducted an ANSYS Fluent study of a Formula Student floor and diffuser across ride heights.
evidence.detail: Coupled CFD results to a simplified suspension model to inform vehicle-level design priorities.

evidence.claim: Built a Python genetic-algorithm workflow coupled to OpenFOAM for undergraduate aerofoil optimisation.
evidence.detail: Automated meshing, batch CFD, objective evaluation and post-processing.

evidence.claim: Supported undergraduate teaching in computer-aided engineering and structural mechanics.
evidence.detail: Experience includes MATLAB numerical methods, SOLIDWORKS, Simulink, flight dynamics and technical guidance.

evidence.claim: Presented computational engineering research to academic and industrial audiences.
evidence.detail: Includes the NGSolve User Meeting 2026 and multiple computational-mechanics conference presentations recorded in the thesis/CV.

evidence.claim: Authored a first-author peer-reviewed paper in Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering related to the PhD work.
evidence.detail: The publication is referenced in current CV/application material.

evidence.claim: Took models through mathematical formulation, implementation, testing, performance assessment and interpretation.
evidence.detail: This full model lifecycle is repeatedly evidenced in PhD and quantitative application materials.

evidence.claim: Investigated discrepancies between numerical implementations and reference simulations by tracing modelling, boundary-condition and numerical assumptions.
evidence.detail: Used in current industrial 3D simulation comparison work.
